html:
November 9, 2026

Articles of impeachment introduced against Defense Secretary Hegseth

tags: politics, defence, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @groundnews, @total.hypocrisy

Republican Rep. Thomas Massie of Kentucky introduced eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Monday, with a House vote expected within days. Three articles concern conducting war against Iran without congressional authorization, and others cover a strike on an Iranian girls' school, boat strikes in the Caribbean and Eastern Pacific, retaliation against Sen. Mark Kelly, the seizure of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro, and operations in Yemen. Impeachment requires a House majority; conviction and removal would require 67 Senate votes. Hegseth told reporters "we're not worried about that" and scheduled his own press conference for Tuesday morning, while Massie called on him to answer each article directly.

Trump questions legitimacy of midterm results after Republican losses

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

President Donald Trump questioned the honesty of the 2026 midterm elections on Truth Social on Monday, six days after Republicans lost ground across the country, including in Texas and South Carolina, and Democrats regained control of both chambers of Congress. He alleged that early voting "dumps" were implausibly large and blamed voting machines, without providing evidence. The claims reverse his statement on election night that he was willing to accept the results and work with Democrats.

Palantir security chief nominated to lead federal cyber agency

tags: surveillance, politics, tech
sources: @total.hypocrisy

The White House on Monday nominated Michael Losapio, chief information security officer at Palantir Technologies, to lead the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency within the Department of Homeland Security. The post has been filled only by acting directors since 2025, and the nomination comes as Senate control is set to change in 2027. Palantir holds a $30 million contract with ICE and supplies tools that track immigration enforcement targets, self-deportations and visa overstays in near real time. The company was co-founded by Peter Thiel, a mentor and donor to Vice President JD Vance.

Eight-year-old taken into ICE custody in San Diego

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

An eight-year-old third grader was taken into ICE custody in San Diego, California, after attending a scheduled immigration meeting. An image circulating shows the boy dressed in a shirt and slacks for the appointment. He did not leave the meeting, and his whereabouts are reported to be unknown.

Trump says US won in Iran and defends strikes on Iranian leadership

tags: war, politics
sources: @ericmoutsos, @oafnation_actual

In a 60 Minutes interview, Trump said the United States had won in Iran and that it was only a question of closing the conflict out now or later, noting that some of Iran's neighbors would prefer the current arrangement and that no American soldiers had been lost. Asked whether he regretted helping Israel carry out decapitation strikes, which the interviewer said prompted escalation, Trump said the US had destroyed Iran's nuclear capability and that some officials wanted to go further. He also said Israel would not exist without the American B-2 strikes on three nuclear sites.

Trump defends foreign-linked business ties and says deportations were too tough

tags: politics, immigration
sources: @ericmoutsos

Pressed on 60 Minutes about World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency company he co-owns that is partly backed by investors connected to the government of the United Arab Emirates, Trump disputed reports his net worth rose by $3 billion and said he knows nothing about the company's dealings. Asked why he does not divest, he said most of his money sits in index funds and that his sons run the family business. In the same interview he said his deportation policy had been too tough, suggested people working in landscaping or hotels should be able to stay, and said a deal with Democrats was doable.

Senate votes on permitting bill that would limit challenges to data centers

tags: politics, tech, climate
sources: @carolinegleich

The Senate was scheduled to vote Monday at 5:30 p.m. Eastern on a bill that would restrict the public's ability to contest construction of data centers and gas pipelines. Changes made over the weekend left in place a provision under which a judge who finds a project broke the law still could not halt it, and the bill shortens the window to bring a court challenge. The vote follows referendums in dozens of towns where voters rejected data center projects.

Supreme Court allows border wall construction to resume near Big Bend

tags: legal, climate, immigration
sources: @carolinegleich

The Supreme Court ruled that border wall construction near Santa Elena Canyon in Big Bend may proceed while litigation continues, lifting an October order by a federal district judge that had paused the work. Bulldozers cleared more than a mile of ground in August under a plan covering about 500 miles of border, which near the canyon includes a new road, surveillance towers and vehicle barriers. An appointed official waived the Endangered Species Act and other protective statutes without a congressional vote. Ranchers, river guides, a church preservation group and five West Texas sheriffs have opposed the project.

Texas governor-elect pledges to end child detention and curb data centers

tags: politics, immigration, tech
sources: @aaronparnas

Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa told The New York Times she will use the state's licensing power to stop private prison companies from detaining children, calling the practice allowed under Governor Abbott child abuse. She also said she would crack down on data centers, extend protections for doctors in the state, and potentially declare an energy emergency and freeze electricity rates.

Fourth senior Justice Department official resigns since the midterms

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Brett Shumate, the assistant attorney general who heads the Justice Department's Civil Division, resigned Monday, as announced by Attorney General Todd Blanche. He is the fourth senior department official to depart since the midterm elections, following Harmeet Dhillon, Jason Reding Quiñones and John Eisenberg.

Trump says he threatened an AI company head with jail

tags: tech, legal, politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Trump said the Justice Department responded to a report of wrongdoing involving artificial intelligence by telling the person to prepare for prison, including remarks about saying goodbye to his wife and children and asking whether he liked the color orange. He declined to name the individual but described him as the head of a major AI company. No details of the alleged misconduct were given.

Nvidia shares slide as Huang apologizes over affair tied to spying allegations

tags: markets, tech
sources: @groundnews

Nvidia closed down 4.3% Monday at $178.59, about 17% below its Oct. 28 close and roughly $890 billion lighter in market value, while the S&P 500 gained 2.4%. The drop followed a Sunday letter from CEO Jensen Huang to staff admitting infidelity, after which the board opened an independent review and national security concerns raised in news reports. Reports named Alice Huang, a Singapore-based Megaspeed executive and no relation, whose firm is accused of routing restricted chips into China; Jensen Huang had lobbied Trump to loosen those export limits. China's Foreign Ministry called the spying allegation unsubstantiated and a smear.

Lauren Boebert loses reelection in Colorado

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual, @groundnews

CNN's Decision Desk projected that Democrat Eileen Laubacher will win Colorado's 4th Congressional District, denying Republican Rep. Lauren Boebert a fourth term. Laubacher is a retired rear admiral with more than 30 years in the Navy who campaigned on living costs. Boebert had switched to a more Republican district in 2024 after winning by 546 votes in 2022, and Trump endorsed her days before the election.

Ukraine and Russia head into US-led talks in Abu Dhabi

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said Monday that Ukrainian battlefield successes and record Russian losses were strengthening Kyiv's position ahead of US-led trilateral talks with Russia opening Tuesday in Abu Dhabi, citing long-range strikes on Russian oil sites. He also said he had spoken with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who told Russia's leader directly that it is time to end the war. Zelenskiy said India is ready to help mediate Black Sea grain export corridors blocked by Russian attacks.

Polish prosecutors treat Kraków shooting as terrorism, motive undetermined

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Polish prosecutors said Monday it was too early to determine whether political ideology motivated the gunman who killed six people and wounded 16 in Kraków on Saturday, and are investigating whether anyone assisted him. Police said Michał Oksiński, 24, died in hospital Monday of wounds from a shootout with officers, and prosecutors say he killed his parents and his 21-year-old sister before driving through the Main Market Square and firing at people. Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said his earlier suggestion that Oksiński held far-right views reflected preliminary leads, a claim Kraków Mayor Łukasz Gibała challenged. Prosecutors confirmed finding a Gadsden flag in Oksiński's room.

Hegseth orders overhaul of US war colleges

tags: defence, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced 33 directives to restructure the US war colleges during an appearance before Naval War College students in Newport on Monday. He said long capstone papers would be replaced by war games. He described the current US strategic shift as deeper than the fall of the Soviet Union.

Russell Brand sentenced to 10 years and six months for rape and sexual assault

tags: legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews

A judge at Southwark Crown Court sentenced Russell Brand on Monday to 10 years and six months in prison after a jury convicted him on Nov. 5 of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault against four women. Mr Justice Joel Bennathan called the 51-year-old a sexual predator who told a series of lies and showed staggering arrogance. The rape conviction involved a 21-year-old he met after a 2009 show at the Hammersmith Apollo, and the assault convictions involved three women between 2004 and 2009. Jurors acquitted him of two further rape counts and one count of attempted indecent assault.

Kenyan pastor sentenced to 200 years over starvation deaths of 190 children

tags: legal
sources: @groundnews

A Mombasa judge sentenced Kenyan pastor Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison on Friday after convicting him of killing 190 children and one adult by directing church members to refuse food. Justice Diana Kavedza found that starvation killed 183 victims while eight deaths were classified as direct homicide, and convicted Mackenzie along with 28 associates who enforced the fasts and buried victims. Investigators recovered more than 400 bodies in 2023 from graves at a ranch in Kilifi County. Separate proceedings involving terrorism, child abuse and torture allegations remain pending.

Newly elected Democratic senators arrive in Washington for orientation

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Newly elected Democratic senators arrived at the Capitol for orientation following the midterm elections. The group includes James Talarico, Josh Turek, Troy Jackson, Peggy Flanagan, Juliana Stratton, Abdul El-Sayed, Adam Hamilton, Annie Andrews of South Carolina, Chris Pappas, Sherrod Brown and Roy Cooper.

Senate Republicans hold prayer meeting after election losses

tags: politics
sources: @aaronparnas

Republican senators led by Sen. Josh Hawley held a Christian prayer meeting following Tuesday's election results. The gathering included a call for a time of fasting and prayer for the nation.

Trump brings UFC head Dana White to the White House briefing podium

tags: politics, media
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Trump called a snap press briefing Monday afternoon and invited UFC head Dana White to speak from the podium. White said he has no political aspirations and described learning of the invitation while in London for a Zuffa boxing event. Questions from reporters included a hypothetical cage match between Trump and former President Joe Biden, which White answered by calling Trump the most resilient person he had met. The briefing came days after Republican losses in the midterm elections.
